hook.text: A franchisor opens a corporate-owned store one mile from your franchise. Your sales drop. It's legal.

buildup.text: Encroachment happens when the franchisor or other franchisees open nearby, cannibalizing your customers.

discovery.text: Many franchise agreements don't protect against encroachment from corporate stores, delivery apps, or e-commerce.

twist.text: Starbucks (company-owned) can open across the street from itself. Franchised brands do the same with loopholes.

climax.text: Encroachment is the most common franchisee complaint. Strong territory clauses are the only protection.

punchline.text: Same brand across the street, owned by corporate. Your sales, their profit.

quiz.question: What is franchise encroachment?
options: The franchisor opening competing locations near existing franchisees

details.summary: Encroachment occurs when a franchisor opens new locations close enough to an existing franchisee to steal their customers and revenue. It is the most contentious issue in franchising, pitting the franchisor's desire for growth and market coverage against franchisees' revenue protection.
details.whyItMatters: Encroachment can destroy a franchisee's investment by splitting their customer base with a new unit. It reveals the fundamental conflict in franchising: franchisors maximize system revenue while individual franchisees need location-level.
takeaways: New same-brand locations near existing ones cannibalize franchisee revenue
Franchisors benefit from more total units even if individual units earn less
Encroachment is the most common source of franchise litigation and conflict

faq.question: Why do franchisors encroach on existing franchisee territories?
faq.answer: Franchisors earn royalties on total system revenue. Two stores generating 600,000 each produce more royalty revenue than one store generating 900,000. The franchisor captures more fees from market saturation even though individual franchisees earn less per location.

faq.question: How can franchisees protect themselves from encroachment?
faq.answer: Negotiate strong exclusive territory clauses before signing. Define territory by population count rather than just geographic radius. Include right of first refusal for new locations in their area. Join franchisee associations that lobby collectively against aggressive expansion plans.
